messages:
alex jensen: Hey team — day 1 here. My company email (alex@redwood.com) doesn't exist yet. I tried signing into Okta and got 'We couldn't find an organization for that email'. No 1Password invite either. Can someone route me?
provisioning-bot: Automated: new_user_provisioning queued for alex.jensen+redwood@gmail.com (steps: Google Workspace create, Okta group sync, 1Password invite). ETA ~10m.
maria: @alex welcome!! I see your hire record. Can you confirm the personal email used for the invite? Also which office/region are you in?
alex jensen: Thanks — alex.jensen+redwood@gmail.com. Remote (EST). No 1Password email in spam. Okta error text was exactly: "We couldn't find an Okta organization for that email."
sam: @alex I'm IT. That message usually means the SSO mapping didn't apply or group sync hasn't hit Okta yet. Can you try signing in directly at https://redwood.okta.com and paste the exact redirect/error text? Also what's your HR ticket number?
alex jensen: Tried direct URL — it redirects to a page that then shows the same 'no org' error. HR ticket is HR-4567. I'm not on any VPN.
sam: Kicked a group sync and forced the SAML mapping for HR-4567. Also resent the 1Password invite to alex.jensen+redwood@gmail.com — check spam and promotions. If Okta still fails I'll create a temporary user so you can at least onboard docs.
linda: Heads up on MFA: once Okta works you'll need to enroll MFA. If you plan to use a YubiKey, we sometimes see issues on M1 Macs with certain hubs — if that happens enroll phone first. @sam I'll stand by to help with any device exceptions.
alex jensen: I just got the 1Password invite — thanks! Okta still shows the same error though.
provisioning-bot: Update: Provisioning step 'Okta org mapping' failed for alex.jensen+redwood@gmail.com. Action required by IT.
sam: Manual fix applied — added you to 'Employees - PMs' and reforced SAML mapping. Try signing in again and let me know.
alex jensen: Success! Signed in and was able to enroll phone MFA. When I plugged in my YubiKey to enroll it I got "device not recognized" on my MacBook Air M1. Anyone seen that?
linda: For M1 machines try: 1) use a direct USB-C port if possible, not a cheap hub; 2) ensure browser has permission in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Input Monitoring / Security; 3) try Chrome if Safari fails. If it still fails, we can provision a temporary passkey or register the key from another machine and then re-register here.
alex jensen: Swapped to a different USB-C adapter and it worked — YubiKey enrolled. Thanks! One more question: how do I get access to PM shared Drive folders?
maria: I'll open a drive access request for you (linking HR-4567). Should be added to the PMs group by EOD. Welcome aboard :tada: If anything else pops up ping #new-hires or @sam.
